  masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is
  being broadcast via teleconference.  Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council
  Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 891 1994 4138 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 891 1994 4138, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order

teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution
Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499 and proposed Resolution 2503, due to the
continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result
of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Accountant Fernando Estrada.

  Accountant Fernando Estrada

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing on the Municipal

  well as regular Ordinance No. 739 adopting the same amendments, and then
  continue the Public Hearing to the next regular meeting; 2) adopt Urgency Ordinance

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted, unlike the recent Accessory Dwelling Unit
legislation, the state Legislature has been silent on the role of Covenants, Conditions, and

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2

 Restrictions (CC&Rs) with respect to SB-9. Community Development & Public Works
Director Wahba estimated that close to half of the City may be part of an HOA with formal

City Attorney Davis explained that any HOAs without formal CC&Rs could consider

City Attorney Davis clarified that the City has not received any applications for lot splits or

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 739 by title.

  “Reducing Short-Lived Climate Pollutants in California” Act.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 740, BECOMING EFFECTIVE
  IMMEDIATELY TO ALIGN WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SB 1383
  “REDUCING SHORT-LIVED CLIMATE POLLUTANTS IN CALIFORNIA” ACT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 22, 2022
 City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 740 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  UPDATED AGREEMENT BETWEEN TURBO DATA SYSTEMS AND THREE
  PENINSULA CITIES (ROLLING HILLS, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, AND RANCHO
  PALOS VERDES) TO PROVIDE PARKING CITATION ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor execute the agreement,
  approved as to form by the City Attorney, between Turbo Data Systems and the three
  Peninsula cities Rolling Hills Estates, Rolling Hills, and Rancho Palos Verdes.

Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Accountant Estrada explained that all issues and complaints would be directly handled by
Turbo Data, and the administration would be handled by Rancho Palos Verdes (RPV), in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that citations would be issued by the
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, then transferred into Turbo Data’s system and
processed for payment by RPV, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT, APPROVED AS
  TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY, BETWEEN TURBO DATA SYSTEMS
  AND THE THREE PENINSULA CITIES ROLLING HILLS ESTATES,
  ROLLING HILLS, AND RANCHO PALOS VERDES.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  VERIZON AGREEMENT MODIFICATIONS AND RENEWAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager execute the
  agreement, between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and Verizon for voice, Internet and
  related services in the amount of $2,328 plus taxes and surcharges per month.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA emphasized that that the City would be getting more speed
for less money with the proposed agreement.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT, BETWEEN
  THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND VERIZON FOR VOICE,
  INTERNET AND RELATED SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $2,328 PLUS
  TAXES AND SURCHARGES PER MONTH.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 22, 2022
 C.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: CLEAN POWER
  ALLIANCE DEFAULT RATE TIER SELECTION (NON-RESIDENTIAL)

  Recommendation: The Environmental Advisory Committee recommends that the City
  Council make no changes to the existing default rate tier of 50% Clean Power for Non-
  Residential accounts and direct staff to launch an educational campaign for the next
  year, promoting the benefits for Non-Residential accounts to opt-up from 50% Clean
  Power to 100% Green Power and report back to the EAC and City Council with the
  results of the respective campaign.

Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported that there was a very good discussion among the
EAC members during the meeting, and summarized the rationale behind both sides of the
Committee’s vote.

Clean Power Alliance Chief Executive Officer Ted Bardacke made comments related to the
proposed change, noting that most customers tend to keep the default rate set by City
Councils.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF stated that she appreciates the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber
of Commerce’s efforts to maintain current rates for local businesses who have suffered
during the pandemic, and supports the recommendation to maintain the 50% default rate
tier for non-residential customers.

Mr. Bardacke discussed participation rates in cities among the various tiers, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN summarized the many environmental changes
occurring globally, noting that he believes this proposed change from 50% to 100% Green
Power for non-residential customers would be the least expensive and most effective
measure that the City will ever be able to take to improve air quality and reduce greenhouse
gas emissions.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that businesses should be able to make their own choices, and
can choose to opt-in if the current rate tier of 50% is maintained.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that if the change was made to 100% Green Power,
business can choose to opt-out.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from Eileen Hupp, President and CEO of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce, in support of the EAC recommendation.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he feels people are not as likely to opt-in if
the 50% default rate tier was maintained.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that she supports the EAC recommendation to
maintain current rates and supports educating businesses so they can make the best choice
for themselves.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she feels moving to the 100% default rate tier
shows leadership, noting that the City can continue to educate, and business would still have
a choice to opt-out should they choose.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR ZERUNYAN, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  MAINTAIN THE EXISTING DEFAULT RATE TIER OF 50% CLEAN POWER
  FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL ACCOUNTS AND DIRECT STAFF TO LAUNCH
  AN EDUCATIONAL CAMPAIGN FOR THE NEXT YEAR, PROMOTING THE
  BENEFITS FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL ACCOUNTS TO OPT-UP FROM 50%

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 22, 2022
   CLEAN POWER TO 100% GREEN POWER AND REPORT BACK TO THE
  EAC AND CITY COUNCIL WITH THE RESULTS OF THE RESPECTIVE
  CAMPAIGN.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Huff, Stegura, and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

The motion failed.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CHANGE THE DEFAULT RATE TIER TO 100% GREEN POWER FOR NON-
  RESIDENTIAL ACCOUNTS, WITH THE OPTION TO OPT-OUT.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, and Zuckerman
  NOES:  Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

The motion carried.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that COVID-19 metrics in Los Angeles County continue to
decline. He noted that the daily positivity rate is 0.6% county-wide, masking requirements have
been lifted in most places other than public transportation and medical-settings, and beginning
April 1 the County will align with the State, lifting vaccine and test-verification requirements for
mega-indoor events.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended the Cal Cities State Board of Directors meeting at the end
of February in Walnut Creek, CA.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also attended the California Contract Cities Association’s (CCCA)
